hobart.intro: Build a Hobart day around the waterfront, museum and a market morning, then leave room for a playground stop in Battery Point.
tips: Start indoors at the Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery: general entry is free. Its regular-season opening days are Tuesday to Sunday; check holiday exceptions before going.
For a weekend outing, choose Salamanca Market on Saturday or Farm Gate Market on Sunday. Their listings link to the published schedules.
Pair the museum with Princes Park when the weather is settled. Take a picnic to keep the outing budget simple.

launceston.intro: Launceston offers an indoor museum day and a Saturday produce-market morning, with two distinct QVMAG sites to choose from.
tips: The QVMAG Museum at Inveresk is at 2 Invermay Road; the Art Gallery at Royal Park is at 2 Wellington Street. Choose the site that suits your interests.
General admission to both sites is free. Planetarium sessions and some programs have separate fees; nearby parking also has charges.
Browse Harvest on Saturday, then choose one museum site for an unhurried afternoon. Check market and museum details before setting out.

judbury.intro: Make Judbury a market-and-park outing: the community market occupies Calvert Park beside the Huon River.
tips: Market days are the second Sunday from September to May, 10 am–2 pm, at 1273 Glen Huon Road. This is a seasonal schedule, so do not assume a winter market.
Combine stalls with the park playground or a riverbank stroll. Council lists free market parking at the recreation oval.
Take a wet-weather layer: stalls are both indoors and outdoors. Check the organiser for cancellations before travelling.

woodbridge.intro: Woodbridge Market brings local makers together at the village hall, making a focused stop for handmade gifts and artisan stalls.
tips: Plan around the organiser’s published calendar rather than assuming the same Sunday every month. January 2027 is listed for the 17th.
Start with the market listing and its organiser link, then browse the wider Channel area for a second stop that fits your day.
Confirm hours and any date changes before travelling. The calendar includes individual dates through September 2027.

liffey.intro: Liffey Valley Market is a seasonal community stop at the old school hall, rather than an every-weekend market.
tips: The published schedule is the second Saturday from September to April, excluding January, 9 am–1 pm.
Use the market listing to check the hall address and the next scheduled dates before choosing your route.
Keep market time and any longer nature outing separate in your plan; check weather and current access information for the outdoor part.

franklin.intro: Franklin’s seasonal market is held at the Palais Theatre, providing a local produce-and-makers stop in the Huon Valley.
tips: The published market pattern is the fourth Sunday, September to May, 10 am–2 pm.
Start at the Palais Theatre market listing, then use the Huon Valley regional catalogue to choose another stop that suits the weather.
Check for cancellations before leaving: a recurring schedule describes the usual market day and is not a guarantee that every session will run.

kingston-beach.intro: Kingston Beach Handmade Market is a monthly makers’ outing centred on the community hall, with the beach as an optional outdoor part of the day.
tips: The published market schedule is the second Sunday, 10 am–3 pm, at the hall on Beach Road.
Browse the handmade stalls first, then decide whether the weather suits time outside. Keep a rain option in your plan.
Check the linked tourism guide and organiser updates before travelling, particularly around holidays.
